_meta.description: 12 circulating misconceptions about reasoning models, paired with the actual position. Source essay: essays/common-misconceptions.md

myths.truth: A chain of thought is tokens emitted by an autoregressive sampler — behavior, not computation. The faithfulness literature shows the chain is often post-hoc and the answer is computed via channels not represented in it.
myths.consequence: Audit by behavior under perturbation, not by reading the chain. CoT-based oversight is weaker than it sounds.

myths.claim: More test-time compute is always better.
myths.truth: The scaling curve is averaged over a distribution. On easy problems, more tokens hurt via overthinking. On problems beyond capability, more compute doesn't close the gap.
myths.consequence: Production systems should condition chain length on estimated difficulty, not emit fixed-length chains.

myths.truth: OpenAI has not described o1 as doing tree search. The system card describes "long internal CoT trained via RL" — sequential sampling, not branching at inference. The MCTS hypothesis is community speculation.
myths.consequence: When citing o1's mechanism, say "long RL-trained CoT" — that's what the source supports.

myths.claim: RL gives the model new reasoning capabilities.
myths.truth: R1-Zero works because the base already contains the reasoning circuits. RL elicits them, raising probability mass on chains that already work. RL on a base too weak to contain the circuits doesn't manufacture new ones.
myths.consequence: Choice of base model is the load-bearing decision. Don't expect RLVR to rescue a weak base.

myths.claim: Chain-of-thought is solved — every model does it well now.
myths.truth: Length, faithfulness, and quality vary widely across models and tasks. Long CoTs hurt on easy tasks. Faithfulness hasn't improved monotonically with model strength. Many small models still fail Wei-style few-shot CoT.
myths.consequence: Empirically test CoT for your task; don't assume it's a solved feature.

myths.truth: Top reasoners are above 80% on AIME-2024 pass@1 — but the test was designed for 15-year-olds, contamination is a documented risk, and per-problem failures are heavily correlated. "Solved" implies generalization that's absent.
myths.consequence: Use FrontierMath, ARC-AGI-2/3, HLE for capability differentiation. AIME is the calibration benchmark, not the frontier.

myths.claim: The chain-of-thought tells you what the model did.
myths.truth: Lanham et al. 2023 and the Anthropic 2025 follow-up show models often reach answers via paths the CoT doesn't mention. Hint-injection studies confirm the chain rationalizes biased answers.
myths.consequence: Don't use CoT inspection as a primary oversight tool for high-stakes deployment.

myths.claim: Search and RL are alternatives. Pick one.
myths.truth: Stream-of-Search (Gandhi et al.) trains search-as-skill. R1's chains contain implicit search behaviors. The most plausible synthesis is that RL absorbs search into the policy, then explicit-search-at-inference adds marginal gains where verifiers are good.
myths.consequence: Treat them as complements; let the verifier quality decide the inference-time mix.

myths.claim: GRPO is the only algorithm that works for reasoning RL.
myths.truth: RLOO, REINFORCE++, plain REINFORCE with smart baselines all report comparable results on open reasoning benchmarks. GRPO is the first algorithm that worked at frontier scale, not provably the best.
myths.consequence: Choose by infrastructure fit and stability, not by algorithm cult.

myths.claim: PRMs are universally better than ORMs.
myths.truth: Lightman et al. 2023 showed PRMs beat ORMs at fixed label budget for verifier training. But: PRMs are expensive to label; AutoPRMs introduce their own noise; using PRMs as RL rewards sometimes destabilizes training. R1 used outcome rewards.
myths.consequence: Default to outcome rewards for RL; reach for PRMs when verifier quality dominates.

myths.claim: Closed-model headline numbers represent the field's state of the art.
myths.truth: Closed-model numbers are vendor-reported, often using bespoke prompting and undisclosed harnesses. Open numbers (R1, Qwen3-Reasoning) are reproducible and frequently within 5-10 points of closed claims for the same benchmark.
myths.consequence: Cite closed numbers as primary-source claims, not as measurements. Compare like with like (open-vs-open, closed-vs-closed).

myths.claim: Distilled R1 models are themselves reasoning models.
myths.truth: R1-Distill-Qwen-7B is a Qwen-7B SFT'd on R1-generated chains. It mimics R1's chain style without RL on it. The reasoning ability transfers to a degree, but it's a SFT model, not an RL-trained reasoner.
myths.consequence: Don't use distilled-R1 results as evidence about the RLVR recipe; use them as evidence about chain-of-thought distillation.
